name: Anbumani Ramadoss
role: Indian former Union health minister (2004–2009) and Pattali Makkal Katchi leader
summary: Ramadoss combines universal public-service proposals and caste-based social-justice advocacy with prohibition and strict criminal penalties. He promotes Tamil-language interests, environmental action and Sri Lankan Tamil self-determination, and personally advocated decriminalising consensual same-sex relations.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He personally promised free healthcare for everyone, financed through revenue reforms rather than consumer giveaways.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He opposed relaxation of factory working-hour limits and defended an eight-hour day as necessary for workers’ health.

cut-welfare.rationale: He condemned dependency-inducing giveaways, while supporting universal services and selected cash benefits.

legalize-drugs.rationale: In April 2026 he promised phased alcohol prohibition and elimination of narcotics; he also advocated banning alcohol consumption in his own 2016 interview.

decide-locally.rationale: His programme devolved executive decisions to five regional administrations.

rehabilitation.rationale: His candidate-led programme made reforming prisoners the goal of prisons.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He criticised the state education policy for failing to require Tamil-medium education.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He urged an immediate national climate emergency and an emergency action plan in Parliament.

state-directs-investment.rationale: His programme directed investment toward industrial corridors and regional development.

right-to-secede.rationale: He urged international support for a referendum on Sri Lankan Tamil self-determination, allowing separation to be considered democratically.

national-self-determination.rationale: He sought a referendum to determine Sri Lankan Tamils’ aspirations for self-determination. The evidence concerns that national conflict specifically.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: His programme offered Sri Lankan refugees facilities equal to local residents.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: His climate plan called for reducing fossil fuels and coal power while expanding renewables.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He sought international action on Sri Lankan wartime crimes and the government’s legal obligations to victims.

death-penalty.rationale: In May 2026 he demanded capital punishment for those responsible for a child’s rape and murder.

minority-language-support.rationale: His programme sought national official status for all 22 scheduled languages.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: His programme reserved half of local-government positions for women.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: His programme withdrew the new pension scheme and restored the old scheme.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: As health minister he personally campaigned to remove Section 377 because criminalisation obstructed HIV prevention and access to gay men.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: His programme recognised transgender women through education and employment reservations.

open-government-data.rationale: His programme published ministerial assessments and draft policies for public feedback.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: He explicitly supported inter-religious marriages, while conditioning his support on women being at least 21.

second-chamber.rationale: His programme restored Tamil Nadu’s legislative upper house.

gm-crops.rationale: He opposed GM mustard release; his campaign proposed a wider GM crop ban.

collective-bargaining.rationale: His October 2026 statement criticised public employers for setting bonuses unilaterally rather than negotiating agreement with trade unions.

student-debt-relief.rationale: His programme waived higher-education loans from public-sector banks.

farm-price-support.rationale: His programme raised state purchase prices for paddy and sugarcane.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: He requested a referendum in Sri Lanka’s north and east to determine the Tamils’ political future.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: He urged India to act internationally to protect Sri Lankan Tamils’ rights and political aspirations.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: His programme removed the additional five-percent surcharge on sugar.

notes: The 2016 programme is attributed because he personally presented it as chief ministerial candidate; programme-only answers remain medium confidence. Later specific statements take precedence. Caste controversies were checked in his full 2013 interview and 2016 interviews; neither opponents’ allegations nor his father’s views are assigned to him. Caste quotas are not silently equated with racial preferences. Support for decriminalisation does not establish support for equal marriage. General free-education promises do not establish the exact scope of university tuition policy. Nuclear questions alone do not establish support for expansion. No living-person inferences are used.
